panels.caption: Brine was a salvage diver off Gull Point. One day his Spark woke in the deep.
He pulled old diving robots off the sea floor and made them his crew.
Then the ghost ship came out of the fog. Sailors jumped ship. Brine took the rest.
Every crate goes to his sea cave. Nobody who went looking ever found it.
You built the suit in Tinker Tess's garage, from scrapyard parts and a dead core.
The core stayed dead until you strapped in. Then it lit up.
Clawback's robots take back anything that glows. Now they want yours.
The core never made your power. It runs on your Spark, and it always has.
Every night BHN 24 tells Brightharbor what happened today. Most of it, anyway.
Some stories never air. Tapes vanish. Screens go black in the middle of a sentence.
Nora Bright has one van, one camera and one uplink the Censor can't reach.
If the uplink holds, every screen in the city shows the truth at once.
Brightharbor: a bright city by the sea, cheering for its famous heroes.
Ten years ago the Spark woke powers in people, and it nearly tore the city apart.
Now Crane Industries scans for the Spark, and Crane's machines hunt anyone who has it.
Today the Spark woke in you. Nobody knows yet. So... who are you?
Ashgrove Labs paid volunteers to sit in the Kindler, a ring of light. Most felt nothing.
Then it was your turn. The ring flashed, and something inside you lit up.
By morning the lab was shut and its files wiped. The director kept testing in secret.
The Kindler never made a Spark. Every powered person has one. It only woke yours.
Three summers without rain. Every farm out here was drying up.
Then my Spark woke up. Anything I touched would grow. Anything!
So I grew a guardian to keep the crows off. It grew. And grew.
Now it's always hungry. But it's MINE. Nobody hurts what I made.
Lark raised her kid brother alone. Patch could fix any radio. Lark could fly.
Then the net vans came. Catchpole hunts Sparks for the bounty on their heads.
Twelve cages in a Docks warehouse. A collar on every Spark, so none can fight back.
For a year Patch searched every radio wave in the city. Tonight one answered.
Years ago, the Crater was a busy city block.
The old heroes made their last stand there against the machines.
Mid-battle, a Crane Industries lab went up in a flash.
When the dust settled, the old heroes were gone. Only the Crater was left.
For years you trained at Master Hoshi's dojo on Willow Street.
Then, one dawn, after a thousand falls, your Spark woke up.
Gale trained just as hard. His Spark never woke, so he built a racing rig.
No one can give you a Spark. Training only wakes the one that was always there.
When the Old Quarry shut down, the Gravel family kept the mine tunnels under it.
Then the eldest son's Spark woke up. His skin turned to quarry stone.
He never lost a fight. So he dug a ring, sold tickets and took the bets.
Lose in the Pit and you owe the family. So you fight again. Nobody walks out.
Long ago a little ship fell from the stars and came down past Radio Hill.
Its pilot stayed, and had a family. The star blood was passed down and down.
This week the old pod woke up, and began to sing to its family.
Its message: every Spark is one Spark. Star blood only woke the one in you.
Forty years ago, Ambrose the Astonishing filled every theatre in Old Town.
His secret was a little relic. Whenever he held it, his Spark woke up.
Jealous Morrow had no Spark. He tried to steal it, so Ambrose vanished for good.
The relic was never magic. It only woke the Spark in its owner. Now that is you.
Sal Scorch started with one tow truck and a lighter. Now his Torch Crew owns the garages.
Pay the Crew, or your shop catches fire. Nobody in Old Town says no twice.
For twenty years Duchess Vanta ran Old Town from the Opal Room. Scorch wants her chair.
So the Duchess wants him gone, by someone nobody in Old Town knows. You.
Long ago Velmara stood in the sun, a city of bronze towers by the bay.
Then a great storm drowned it. Its people swam for the shore and never came back.
They left the Tidewright to keep the city safe. It waited, and waited, and slept.
Last week a salvage drill cracked the seal. The guardian woke up angry.
Tick-Tock Toys was my favourite shop. The Toymaker said I was special.
He gave me a wind-up bear. When I cried, every toy on the street woke up!
Then he broke my toys on purpose. Every day. So I would keep crying.
His machine in the basement drinks it all up. He calls it the Tantrum Tap.
For twelve years Lodestar and Vesper kept Brightharbor's night sky safe.
After every patrol: the Night Owl diner, two coffees, the booth by the window.
Then the harbour fire, last winter. Vesper flew in for the last family and never came out.
Last month she was back: rich, famous, on every screen. She walked right past him.
Halo Academy said I was special. Free lessons for kids with Sparks.
Headmaster Halo picked me for the honours class. Everyone clapped.
Downstairs, a machine measured my Spark. A robot stood up... with MY powers.
So I ran. And I kept running until I found you.
